steps: Cooking the beans: Boil the 500g black-eyed peas for 20-25 minutes until tender. Black-eyed peas don't need overnight soaking like other legumes, which is why this is a quick dish.
Draining: Drain the beans well, reserving a little of the cooking water in case you need to thin the sauce later.
Sautéing the onion: In a pot, heat a little of the olive oil and sauté the finely chopped onion until glossy and softened. Sautéing adds sweetness and depth of flavor.
Adding the tomato: Add the 2 finely chopped tomatoes, the celery leaves, and the drained beans. Season with salt and pepper. The celery gives the dish its characteristic fresh aroma.
Simmering: Simmer for about 10 minutes so the flavors meld and the liquid reduces slightly. Important: add the main portion of salt toward the end, since adding it earlier can toughen the bean skins.
Finishing: Off the heat, add the lemon juice and the remaining raw olive oil. The raw oil and lemon added at the end preserve a fresh aroma and flavor that would be lost with cooking. Serve warm.
mavromatika.plate: With olive oil, lemon, and fresh spring onion. A Lenten dish.

steps: Prepping the ingredients: Make sure the 1 egg is at room temperature. Important: a room-temperature egg is the secret to success, since it binds with the oil more easily into a stable emulsion.
Base in the jar: Crack the egg into the tall cup of an immersion blender and add the 1 tbsp lemon juice, the 1 tsp Dijon mustard, salt, and white pepper.
Adding the oil: Pour in all the oil on top — the 200ml sunflower oil and the 50ml olive oil — without stirring. The oil will rise and settle above the egg.

First blend: Place the immersion blender's shaft at the bottom of the cup, right over the egg, and blend on high speed without moving the shaft for about 10 seconds. This is how the emulsion starts to set from the bottom up.
Raising the blender: Very slowly begin raising the shaft, gradually incorporating the oil. You'll see the mayonnaise thicken and set into a white cream.
Adjusting and storing: Taste and adjust the salt and lemon. Store in a sealed container in the refrigerator for up to 5 days, since it contains raw egg.
mayoneza.plate: In a bowl, a thin drizzle of olive oil on top for presentation.

steps: Prepping the eggplants: Pierce the 3 large eggplants in several places with a fork so steam can escape and they don't burst while roasting.

Roasting: Roast the eggplants directly over an open flame or under the oven grill for 15-20 minutes, turning them, until the skin is charred all over and the flesh inside is completely softened. Roasting over fire gives the salad its characteristic smoky aroma.
Peeling: Let the eggplants cool slightly, then peel them carefully, removing all the charred skin so no bitterness remains.

Draining the liquid: Squeeze the flesh well or let it drain in a colander to remove excess liquid. Important: this is the secret to keeping the eggplant dip from turning watery and giving it a thick, creamy texture.

Mixing: Finely chop or mash the flesh with a fork and mix with 2 crushed garlic cloves, 1 tbsp lemon juice, the 3 tbsp olive oil, and salt. Add the olive oil gradually while stirring so it emulsifies and becomes light and fluffy.
Serving: Sprinkle with chopped parsley and serve with fresh bread or pita. Taste and adjust salt or lemon to preference.
melitzanosalata.plate: In a bowl, drizzle with olive oil, garnish with parsley, serve with bread.

steps: Beating the liquids: Beat the 150ml olive oil with the 100g sugar until well combined. Add the 120ml orange juice, the cinnamon and cloves, which give the festive aroma.

Adding the flour: Sift the 500g flour together with 1 tsp baking soda and gradually combine it with the liquids. IMPORTANT: knead lightly, only as much as needed to bring the dough together, since over-kneading toughens the melomakarona.
Shaping: Shape oval cookies of even size and place them on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper, leaving space between them as they'll puff up slightly.
Piercing: Lightly prick each cookie with a fork, so they bake evenly through and absorb the syrup better later.
Baking: Bake at 180°C for 20-25 minutes until golden and firm. They need to be well baked so they don't turn mushy in the syrup.
Making the syrup: Boil the 200g honey with the 200ml water (1:1 ratio) for a few minutes to make a thin honey syrup.
Syruping: IMPORTANT: dip the warm melomakarona into the syrup (or hot syrup over cold cookies), 1-2 times. The temperature contrast helps them absorb the syrup without falling apart.
Finishing: Drain them and sprinkle with ground walnuts and cinnamon on top. Let them stand a few hours to fully absorb the syrup.
melomakarona.plate: On a platter, sprinkled with walnuts and cinnamon.

steps: Drain the mizithra in a cloth for 2 hours if it is at all wet.
Important: Wet mizithra never sets and the melopita comes out of the oven as a soft puddle.
Press the pastry base into a round tin and prick it all over with a fork so it does not puff up.
Pass the mizithra through a sieve or beat it until completely smooth with no lumps.
Warm the honey slightly so it flows, then beat it into the cheese.
Add the eggs one at a time, beating well after each, and finally the flour.
Important: Do not over-beat. Too much air makes the filling rise dramatically and then collapse and crack as it cools.
Pour the filling into the base and smooth the surface.
Bake at 170°C for 50-60 minutes, until set at the edges with a slight wobble in the centre.
Let it cool completely in the tin, dust generously with cinnamon and serve at room temperature.
melopita_sifnou.plate: Serve in pieces at room temperature, with plenty of cinnamon on top.

steps: Puff pastry: Roll out the puff pastry sheet on parchment paper and prick it well with a fork so it doesn't puff up unevenly.
Baking: Bake at 200°C for 15-18 minutes until golden, placing a second sheet of parchment paper and a baking tray on top to keep it flat.
Important: The pastry must be baked all the way through and cooled completely before cutting, otherwise it will shatter badly and won't form clean layers.
Pastry cream: Whisk the egg yolks with the sugar and cornstarch until pale.
Cooking the cream: Heat the milk with the vanilla and gradually add it to the mixture, stirring constantly over low heat until it thickens.
Finishing the cream: Remove from the heat, add the butter, stir, and cover with plastic wrap pressed directly onto the surface to prevent a skin from forming.
Whipping the cream: Whip the heavy cream to soft peaks and gently fold it into the cooled pastry cream.
Assembly: Cut the pastry into three equal pieces and layer alternately: pastry-cream-pastry-cream-pastry.
Finishing: Dust the top with powdered sugar or decorate with melted chocolate drizzled in stripes.
Chilling: Let the mille-feuille chill in the refrigerator for at least 2 hours before cutting, so it sets properly.
milfey.plate: Serve cold on a platter, cut into square pieces, dusted with powdered sugar

ing: Powdered sugar for the icing 150 g
steps: Preparing the pastry: Unroll the puff pastry sheets and place them on parchment-lined baking trays, pricking them well with a fork so they don't puff up excessively.
Baking: Bake the sheets in a preheated oven at 200°C for 15-18 minutes, until golden and crisp. Let cool completely on a rack.
Important: To keep the pastry flat and crisp, place a second tray on top during baking, so it is pressed lightly and doesn't rise unevenly.
Pastry cream: Heat the milk in a saucepan. In a bowl, whisk the yolks with the sugar and cornstarch until the mixture turns pale.

Cooking the cream: Slowly pour the hot milk into the egg mixture, stirring constantly, return to the heat and stir until the cream thickens. Add the vanilla and let cool covered with plastic wrap pressed onto the surface.
Whipping the cream: Whip the heavy cream and gently fold it into the cold pastry cream to make it lighter.
Assembly: Cut the pastry sheets into equal rectangles. Layer one sheet, spread cream generously, place a second sheet, more cream, and finish with a third sheet.

Icing and decoration: Make an icing by mixing powdered sugar with a few drops of lemon juice and water until slightly thickened. Spread it over the surface and pipe stripes of melted chocolate, dragging a toothpick through for the classic pattern.
Chilling: Place the dessert in the refrigerator for at least 1 hour before cutting, so the cream sets and it slices cleanly.
millefeuille_franc.plate: Serve cold on a plate with a little powdered sugar and fresh forest berries on the side

ing: Sugar 200 g (150 g for the filling, 50 g for the dough)
Cinnamon 1 tsp + a little grated nutmeg
steps: Dough: In a bowl, mix the flour with the baking powder and the 50 g of sugar. Add the cold butter cut into cubes and rub it in with your fingertips until the mixture resembles coarse breadcrumbs. Add 1 egg and bring the dough together without overworking it.
Important: Wrap the dough in plastic wrap and chill in the refrigerator for at least 30 minutes. The cold butter and resting time make the dough crisp and short (shortcrust) rather than tough.
Filling: Peel the apples, cut them into thin slices or cubes and immediately sprinkle with lemon juice to prevent browning. Add the zest, the 150 g of sugar, cinnamon and a little nutmeg.
Sautéing: In a frying pan, sauté the apples with the sugar for 8-10 minutes, until they soften and caramelize slightly and their liquid evaporates. Let cool and add the walnuts.
Rolling out: Divide the dough into two portions (2/3 and 1/3). Roll out the larger piece with a rolling pin and line a buttered baking pan or tin, covering the sides as well.

Filling: Pour in the apple filling and level it out. Roll out the remaining piece of dough and cover the pie, sealing the edges well. Cut 2-3 slits in the top to let steam escape and brush with beaten egg.
Baking: Bake in a preheated fan oven at 180°C for 40-45 minutes, until the top turns golden brown.
Serving: Let the apple pie cool a little so the filling sets, dust with powdered sugar and cut into pieces.
milopita.wine: Sweet Samos wine or a hot cinnamon tea.
milopita.plate: Serve warm with a scoop of vanilla ice cream, dusted with cinnamon.

steps: Peel the apples, cut them into small cubes and toss them at once with the lemon juice so they do not brown.
Mix in the sugar, cinnamon, raisins and chopped walnuts.
Important: Let the filling stand in a sieve for 20 minutes and discard the juice it releases. This liquid is exactly what turns the pastry to mush.
Toast the breadcrumbs in a little butter until golden — they sit under the filling and absorb any remaining moisture.
Lay out a sheet of phyllo, brush it with melted butter and repeat, stacking all six sheets.
Scatter the toasted breadcrumbs along one long edge and pile the filling on them, leaving a clear border all around.
Fold the two short sides inwards first, then roll it up firmly like a Swiss roll, without gaps.
Place it seam-side down on a lined tray, brush the surface generously with butter and score it in portions.
Bake at 180°C for 40-45 minutes, until deep golden and crisp.
Rest for 15 minutes, then dust with icing sugar and cut along the scored lines.
milopita_rolo.plate: Serve in warm slices, dusted with icing sugar and a scoop of vanilla ice cream.

steps: Sauté the onion, garlic, carrots and celery for 5 minutes.
Add the tomato, stock, salt and pepper. Simmer for 15 minutes.
Add the zucchini and beans. Cook for 10 minutes.
Add the pasta and simmer for another 10 minutes.
Serve with parmesan and basil.

ing: Coarsely chopped walnuts or almonds 60 g (optional)
steps: Breaking the biscuits: Break the biscuits by hand into small, irregular pieces in a large bowl. Important: Don't turn them into powder in a blender. The irregular pieces are what give the cross-section its mosaic (salami) look that's characteristic of this dessert. Add the walnuts too if using.

Melting the chocolate: Melt the chocolate with the butter in a bain-marie (a bowl over a saucepan of gently simmering water, without the bottom touching the water), stirring until smooth. Remove from heat and let cool slightly.
Cocoa cream: In another bowl, beat the egg with the sugar until fluffy. Stir in the cocoa and evaporated milk and mix well so there are no lumps.
Combining the mixtures: Pour the melted chocolate into the egg mixture, stirring constantly, and finally add the cognac. The mixture should be smooth and glossy.
Mixing with the biscuits: Pour the chocolate cream over the broken biscuits and gently fold with a spatula until all the pieces are coated, keeping them intact.

Rolling into a log: Turn the mixture out onto plastic wrap or parchment paper and, gathering the edges, shape it into a compact log (salami shape). Roll it up tightly and twist the ends like a candy wrapper to hold its shape.
Chilling: Put the log in the refrigerator for at least 4-5 hours (ideally overnight) so it firms up completely and slices cleanly.
Serving: Unwrap, dust with a little powdered sugar if you want the salami look, and cut into slices about 1 cm thick with a sharp knife.
mosaiko.wine: Sweet Mavrodafni wine or an espresso.
mosaiko.plate: In slices on a small plate, dusted with powdered sugar.

steps: Preparing the okra: Carefully trim the stem ends of the 500g okra without piercing the pods, sprinkle with 2 tbsp vinegar and let sit for 30 minutes. Important: the vinegar removes the okra's sliminess, keeping the pods whole and preventing them from turning the dish mushy.
Browning the beef: In a pot with a little olive oil, brown the 600g cubed beef on all sides over high heat. Caramelization seals in the juices and adds depth of flavor.
Sautéing the aromatics: Add 1 finely chopped onion and 2 garlic cloves and sauté until softened, scraping up the caramelized bits from the bottom.

Simmering the meat: Add the 400g grated tomato and a little hot water, salt and pepper. Cover and simmer for 40 minutes, until the beef begins to become tender. The meat needs more time to cook than the okra.

Adding the okra: Rinse the vinegar off the okra and lay the pods over the meat. Important: from this point on, don't stir with a spoon — just gently shake the pot, since stirring will break up and mash the okra.
Finishing: Continue cooking for another 25 minutes over low heat (or in the oven), until the okra is tender and the sauce has thickened.
Serving: Let the dish rest briefly and serve lukewarm, as bamies and other olive-oil-based dishes taste best not piping hot, with fresh bread and feta.
mosxari_bamies.plate: In a deep plate, okra on top, with bread.

steps: Preparing the meat: Pat the beef dry well with paper towels and pierce it in several places with a sharp knife to stuff the holes with garlic.
Marinating: Make a mixture of olive oil, lemon juice, mustard, oregano, salt and pepper and rub the meat well on all sides.
Searing the meat: Important: First sear the beef over high heat in a pot with a little oil until well browned on all sides, so the pores 'close' and the meat retains its juices during roasting.
Placing in the pan: Put the meat in a baking pan, add the bay leaves and water or stock, cover tightly with foil and roast in a preheated oven at 180°C for about 1.5-2 hours.
Adding the potatoes: Peel the potatoes, cut them into slices or chunks, season with salt, pepper, oregano and oil, and add them around the meat halfway through roasting.
Final roasting: Remove the foil for the last 30 minutes and raise the temperature to 200°C to brown the meat and potatoes, basting regularly with the pan juices.
Resting the meat: Important: Once out of the oven, let the beef rest covered for 10-15 minutes before carving, so the juices redistribute and it stays juicy.
Serving: Slice the meat against the grain and serve with the potatoes and the pan sauce on top.
mosxari_fournou_patates.wine: Xinomavro from Naoussa or another full-bodied dry red wine.
mosxari_fournou_patates.plate: Serve on a platter with the potatoes around the meat and plenty of sauce on top, accompanied by Greek village salad.

steps: Preparing the meat: Keep the beef in one whole piece, dry it thoroughly and season it heavily with salt and pepper on every side.
Searing: Sear it in the pot over high heat with oil until dark brown all over, about 3 minutes per side.
Sautéing the aromatics: Add the whole onions, the garlic and the carrots cut into thick chunks and sauté for 5 minutes.
Deglazing: Pour in the wine and let it evaporate, then add the grated tomato, the rosemary and the bay leaves.
Sealing the pot: Important: The gastra works because it is completely sealed — if the lid is not tight, lay a sheet of foil under it so no steam escapes.
Slow cooking: Cook over very low heat, or in the oven at 160°C, for 2 hours without opening the pot. Every time you lift the lid you lose the steam that is doing the work.
Adding the potatoes: Add the potatoes cut into large chunks, season, reseal and cook for another 45 minutes.
Checking: The meat is done when a fork slides in and out with no resistance and the potatoes have absorbed the sauce.
Resting and carving: Let it rest for 15 minutes, then carve the meat into thick slices against the grain.
mosxari_gastra.wine: A rustic red — Agiorgitiko, Mavrodaphne dry or a Naoussa Xinomavro.
mosxari_gastra.plate: Serve family-style straight from the pot, with the meat sliced in the centre and the vegetables around it.

steps: Browning the meat: Heat olive oil and brown the 800g beef on all sides over high heat, then remove it from the pot. Important: browning locks in the juices and gives the sauce a rich flavor.
Sautéing the aromatics: In the same oil, sauté the 2 chopped onions and the 3 cloves of garlic for 3 minutes until softened.
Deglazing with wine: Add the 150ml red wine and let the alcohol evaporate, scraping the bottom to release the caramelized bits.
Adding the remaining ingredients: Add the 400g grated tomato, the cinnamon stick, the 3 cloves, the 2 bay leaves, and a little water, then return the meat to the pot.
Simmering: Cover and simmer for 75-80 minutes until the meat is fork-tender, adding hot water if needed so it doesn't dry out.
Finishing: Season with salt and pepper at the end, remove the bay leaves and cinnamon stick, and serve with potatoes or pasta.
mosxari_kokkinisto.plate: With pasta or rice, plenty of sauce.

steps: Browning the beef: Pat dry the 800g beef, cut into pieces, and brown on all sides over high heat in olive oil. Set aside. Important: a good sear creates a caramelized crust that gives deep, rich flavor to the finished dish.
Sautéing the onions: In the same pot, sauté the 500g whole pearl onions until golden. Light caramelization sweetens the onions and balances the acidity of the sauce.

Deglazing and spices: Deglaze with the 200ml red wine and the 2 tbsp vinegar, scraping up the browned bits from the bottom. Add the 400g grated tomato, the 3 garlic cloves, the cinnamon stick, the 4 cloves and the 2 bay leaves. Let the alcohol evaporate so the wine loses its bitterness.
Slow cooking: Return the meat to the sauce, cover and simmer gently for 70-80 minutes over low heat. Slow cooking breaks down the beef's connective tissue and makes it melt in your mouth.

Reducing the sauce: Season with salt and pepper toward the end. Important: if the sauce is too thin, remove the lid for the last 15 minutes so the liquid evaporates and the sauce turns glossy and clings to the meat.
Serving: Serve the stifado hot with the onions whole, alongside hilopites (Greek egg noodles) or mashed potatoes that soak up the sauce beautifully.
mosxari_stifado.plate: With rice or bread, plenty of sauce.

steps: Preparing the fillet: Tie the fillet with kitchen string every 3-4 cm so it holds an even cylindrical shape, and season it generously with salt and pepper.

Searing: Sear the fillet in a very hot pan with oil for 1-2 minutes per side, until a dark crust forms all over. Important: the pan must be smoking hot — this crust is pure flavour and it also seals the surface.
Brushing with mustard: While the fillet is still warm, brush it all over with the Dijon mustard and let it cool completely. A warm fillet would melt the pastry later.
Making the duxelles: Blitz the mushrooms and shallots in a food processor until finely minced, then cook them in the butter over medium heat for about 15 minutes.
Drying the duxelles: Important: Keep cooking until every drop of moisture has evaporated and the mixture pulls away from the pan. Any remaining water will turn the pastry to mush.
Flavouring: Add the brandy and the thyme leaves, cook for 2 more minutes to burn off the alcohol, season and let it cool completely.
Building the layers: Lay out cling film, arrange the prosciutto slices overlapping into a rectangle, spread the duxelles evenly over them and place the fillet at one edge.
Rolling: Roll tightly using the cling film into a firm cylinder, twist the ends like a sweet wrapper and chill for 30 minutes so it sets its shape.
Wrapping in pastry: Unwrap the cylinder onto the puff pastry sheet, roll it up, seal the edges well and place it seam-side down on a lined baking tray.
Chilling: Chill the parcel for another 20 minutes. Cold pastry rises higher and crisper in the oven.
Baking: Brush with the egg yolk, score the surface lightly with a knife and bake at 200°C for 35-40 minutes for medium doneness.
Resting: Important: Let it rest for 10 minutes before slicing. Cutting immediately would let all the juices run out onto the board.
mosxari_wellington.wine: A serious red — aged Bordeaux, Nemea Grande Reserve or a full-bodied Xinomavro.
mosxari_wellington.plate: Slice into thick rounds with a serrated knife and serve on warm plates with a red wine sauce and glazed vegetables.

steps: Chill the cream, the bowl and the whisk in the freezer for 10 minutes — cold equipment is what lets cream whip properly.
Whip the cream to soft peaks, stopping before it turns grainy.
In a separate bowl mix the condensed milk with the lemon zest.
Important: Add the lemon juice slowly while stirring. The acid thickens the condensed milk on contact, and pouring it in at once creates lumps that never smooth out.
Fold the lemon mixture into the whipped cream with a spatula, using gentle upward strokes to keep the air in.
Divide into glasses and refrigerate for at least 4 hours until set.
Serve chilled with a little extra zest on top.
mous_lemoniou.wine: A Muscat of Lemnos or a sweet sparkling wine.
mous_lemoniou.plate: Serve in clear glasses with lemon zest and a mint leaf.

steps: Preparing the eggplant: Cut the eggplants into slices about 1 cm thick. Salt them generously and let them sit in a colander for 30 minutes — the salt draws out bitterness and excess moisture, so they won't soak up oil and turn the moussaka watery. Rinse and pat them very dry with paper towels.

Roasting the vegetables: Brush the eggplant and the potatoes (sliced 0.5 cm thick) with a little olive oil and roast at 200°C for 20-25 minutes until softened and lightly browned. Roasting instead of frying keeps the dish lighter. Set aside.

Sautéing the onion: In a wide pot, heat 2-3 tbsp olive oil over medium heat and sauté the finely chopped onion for 5-6 minutes until glossy and softened — don't let it burn, we want sweetness, not bitterness.

Browning the meat: Raise the heat, add the ground beef, and break it up with a spoon. Sauté for 8-10 minutes until its liquid evaporates and it browns — this stage builds depth of flavor as the meat's sugars caramelize.

Meat sauce: Deglaze with half a glass of wine (optional) and let it evaporate for 1-2 minutes. Add the grated tomato, a cinnamon stick (or 1/2 tsp ground), salt, pepper, and a little sugar to cut the acidity. Simmer uncovered for 20-25 minutes until it thickens and stops releasing liquid.

Béchamel: Melt 80g butter in a pot, add the flour, and stir for 1-2 minutes to cook it (making a roux — it must not brown). Gradually add the hot milk, whisking constantly so it doesn't lump. Cook until it thickens to a custard-like consistency. Remove from heat, add a little nutmeg, and once slightly cooled, whisk in 2 eggs and a handful of grated kefalotyri.

Assembly: In a baking pan, layer the potatoes first (the base that holds the juices), then half the eggplant, all the meat sauce, the remaining eggplant, and finally all the béchamel spread evenly. Sprinkle cheese on top.

Baking & resting: Bake at 180°C for 50-60 minutes, until the béchamel turns golden and forms a crust. IMPORTANT: let the moussaka cool for at least 20-30 minutes before cutting it — otherwise it will fall apart. Cut into squares and serve.
Melt the chocolate with the butter over a bain-marie or in the microwave. Let it cool slightly.
Beat the egg yolks with the sugar until pale. Stir into the chocolate.
Whip the heavy cream into whipped cream. Whip the egg whites into stiff peaks.
Fold the whipped cream into the chocolate first with gentle movements, then fold in the meringue. Important: do not stir vigorously — the air is what gives the mousse its light, airy texture.
Divide among glasses or bowls and chill for 3-4 hours.
Serve with grated chocolate or whipped cream.
Preparing the meat: Put the ground beef in a bowl with salt and freshly ground pepper, and knead lightly just enough to combine, without overworking it, so it stays tender.
Shaping the patties: Divide the meat into 4 equal balls and flatten them into patties about 2 cm thick, slightly wider than the buns since they will shrink during cooking.
Important: Press a small indentation in the center of each patty with your thumb, so it doesn't puff up during cooking and stays flat.
Heating the pan: Heat the pan or grill well over high heat with a little olive oil before adding the patties, so they caramelize immediately.
Cooking: Cook the patties for 3-4 minutes per side for medium doneness, flipping only once to keep their juices.
Cheese: One minute before removing the patties, place a slice of cheese on top and cover the pan so it melts gently.
Buns: Split the buns in half and toast them briefly on the grill, cut side down, until lightly browned.
Assembling: Spread mustard and ketchup on the bottom bun, add lettuce, the cheese-topped patty, tomato slices, onion, and pickles, then close with the top bun.
mpourger_spitiko.wine: Ice-cold lager beer or a light dry red wine
mpourger_spitiko.plate: Serve with french fries and barbecue sauce on the side.

ing: Fresh mussels in the shell 1 kg
Freshly ground pepper and salt, used sparingly
steps: Cleaning: Wash the mussels well under cold running water, scrubbing the shells and pulling out the "beards" (the fibrous threads). Discard any mussels that are cracked or open and don't close when tapped lightly.
Important: use only live mussels. Before cooking, any open shell must close with a light tap, otherwise the mussel is dead and must be discarded, as it can cause food poisoning.
Sautéing: In a wide pot, heat the olive oil over medium heat and sauté the chopped onion until softened. Add the chopped garlic and stir for a minute, until fragrant, without letting it burn.

Deglazing with wine: Pour in the white wine and let it come to a boil for 1-2 minutes so the alcohol evaporates. If using, add the grated tomato and cook for 3-4 minutes until the sauce thickens slightly.
Steaming: Raise the heat, add the mussels to the pot, and cover immediately with the lid. Shake the pot while holding the lid so the juices circulate and the mussels cook evenly.
Cooking time: Leave the mussels covered for 4-6 minutes, until all the shells have opened. Don't overcook them, or the flesh will toughen and become rubbery.

Checking: Discard any mussels that remain closed after cooking, as they are not safe to eat. Taste the broth and season with salt and freshly ground pepper sparingly, keeping in mind that mussels are naturally salty.
Finishing: Turn off the heat, add the lemon juice, and sprinkle with plenty of chopped parsley. Stir gently and serve immediately, while still hot and steaming.
mydia_axnista.wine: Dry, crisp white, such as Assyrtiko or Moschofilero.
mydia_axnista.plate: Serve in a deep bowl with their broth and plenty of fresh bread for dipping into the sauce. Accompany with a lemon wedge.

steps: Cleaning the mussels: Thoroughly clean the 1kg mussels, scrubbing the shells and removing the beards. Important: discard any mussels that are open and don't close when tapped, as they are not fresh.
Opening the mussels: In a covered pot with a little water, cook the mussels over high heat for 3-4 minutes until they open. Discard any that don't open, as they aren't safe to eat.
Preparing the sauce: In a pan with olive oil, sauté 2 garlic cloves, then add the 200g grated tomato and a little finely chopped hot pepper.
Deglazing with ouzo: Add the 3 tbsp ouzo and let the alcohol evaporate, leaving behind only the anise aroma that pairs so well with seafood.
Simmering the sauce: Simmer the sauce for 5 minutes until it thickens slightly and the flavors meld.
Combining: Add the mussels to the sauce and stir gently to coat them, adding a little of their liquid for extra flavor.
Finishing and serving: Grate the 80g feta over the top and sprinkle with parsley. Serve immediately while piping hot, so the mussels stay juicy.
mydia_saganaki.plate: Deep plate or saganaki pan, with fresh bread.

steps: Cutting the vegetables: Finely chop the half onion, 1 pepper, and 1 tomato. Even, fine chopping helps them sauté quickly and cook together.
Sautéing: Sauté the vegetables in 2 tbsp olive oil for 3-4 minutes until softened. Important: let the tomato release its liquid so the omelet doesn't turn watery while cooking.
Beating the eggs: Beat the 4 eggs with salt, pepper, and the 30g grated cheese until combined. A little beating incorporates air and makes the omelet fluffier.
Adding the mixture: Pour the beaten eggs into the pan over the vegetables, over medium-low heat. High heat burns the bottom before the top cooks.
Cooking: Cover the pan for 3-4 minutes until the surface sets. The lid traps steam and cooks the omelet from the top as well.
Flipping and serving: If you like, flip the omelet for a few seconds on the other side and serve hot immediately.
